notes.definition: Distance is how far an object moves along its path; it is a scalar with no direction. Displacement is the distance moved in a straight line from the start point to the finish point, together with the direction of that line; it is a vector.
explanation: Distance tells you how far an object has travelled. If you walk to school along winding roads, the distance is the total length of the route you actually followed. Distance does not involve direction, so it is a scalar quantity: it only has a size (magnitude). Distance is measured in metres (m), although kilometres (km) are often used for long journeys.

Displacement is different. It is measured in a straight line from where the object started to where it finished, and it must include the direction of that straight line. Because it has both magnitude and direction, displacement is a vector quantity. A displacement is not complete without a direction: "5 m" is not a displacement, but "5 m east" or "5 m at a bearing of 090°" is.

For motion along a straight line, it often helps to choose one direction as positive. If a person walks 8 m east and then 3 m west, the distance travelled is 8 + 3 = 11 m. The displacement is 8 − 3 = 5 m east, because they finish 5 m east of their starting point. If east is positive, a displacement of −5 m would mean 5 m west.

Distance can only stay the same or increase as an object moves, but displacement can go up, go down or return to zero. A runner who completes exactly one lap of a 400 m track has travelled a distance of 400 m but has a displacement of zero, because they finish where they started. A ball thrown 3 m straight up that lands back in the thrower's hand travels 6 m but has zero displacement.

The size of the displacement can never be larger than the distance travelled. The two are equal only when the object moves in a straight line without changing direction. Any turning, reversing or curved path makes the distance larger than the displacement. This difference between a scalar and its matching vector is also true for speed (scalar) and velocity (vector), which you meet next.

To express a displacement fully, give both the magnitude with units and the direction. Directions can be given as compass points (north, south, east, west), as a bearing, as up or down, as left or right, or as a positive or negative sign once a positive direction has been chosen. Vectors can be shown as arrows: the length of the arrow represents the magnitude and the arrow points in the direction.
keyFacts: Distance is how far an object moves; it does not involve direction.
Distance is a scalar quantity: it has magnitude only.
Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish plus the direction of that line.
Displacement is a vector quantity: it has magnitude and direction.
Both distance and displacement are measured in metres (m).
A displacement must always be given with a direction, for example 40 m north.
If an object returns to its starting point, its displacement is zero but the distance travelled is not.
The magnitude of displacement is never greater than the distance travelled.
Distance and displacement have the same size only for motion in one direction along a straight line.
A vector can be drawn as an arrow: length shows magnitude, the arrowhead shows direction.

keyTerms.definition: How far an object moves along its path. A scalar quantity measured in metres.
The distance in a straight line from the start point to the finish point, together with the direction. A vector quantity.
A quantity that has magnitude (size) only, for example distance, speed, mass, time.
A quantity that has both magnitude and direction, for example displacement, velocity, force.
The size of a quantity, for example the 5 m in "5 m east".
Which way a vector points, given as a compass direction, bearing, up/down, or a positive or negative sign.

workedExamples.title: Back and forth along a straight line
workedExamples.question: A dog runs 25 m east to fetch a ball, then runs 10 m west towards its owner. Calculate (a) the distance travelled and (b) the displacement of the dog.
steps: Distance ignores direction, so add the two lengths: 25 m + 10 m = 35 m.
For displacement, take east as positive: +25 m + (−10 m) = +15 m.
A positive answer means east, so the displacement is 15 m east.

workedExamples.title: Returning to the start
workedExamples.question: A lift carrying a cleaner goes up 24 m from the ground floor to the top floor, then comes back down to the ground floor. State the distance travelled and the displacement of the lift.
steps: Distance: 24 m up + 24 m down = 48 m.
The lift finishes at the same point it started, so the straight line from start to finish has zero length.
Displacement = 0 m (no direction is needed for a zero displacement).

workedExamples.title: Moving at right angles (Higher challenge)
workedExamples.question: A walker goes 300 m north and then 400 m east. Calculate the distance walked and the magnitude of the displacement.
steps: The displacement is the straight line from start to finish. The two walks are at right angles, so use Pythagoras: displacement² = 300² + 400².
The direction is north east of the start (between north and east), so the displacement is 500 m in a north-easterly direction.
workedExamples.answer: Distance 700 m; displacement 500 m (towards the north east)

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think distance and displacement are just two names for the same thing.
misconceptions.right: In fact distance is the length of the path actually travelled (a scalar), while displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish with a direction (a vector). They are only equal in size for straight-line motion in one direction.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a displacement can be given as a number and a unit, such as 60 m.
misconceptions.right: In fact a displacement must include a direction, for example 60 m south. Without a direction it is only a distance.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think that if an object has travelled a long way, its displacement must be large.
misconceptions.right: In fact an object can travel a large distance and end up with zero displacement if it returns to its starting point, like a runner completing a lap.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a negative displacement means the object moved a negative distance.
misconceptions.right: In fact the negative sign only shows direction: the object finished on the opposite side of the start to the direction chosen as positive.

realWorld: Sat-navs and map apps show the road distance for a journey, which is longer than the straight-line distance (the size of the displacement) between start and destination.
In a 400 m race on a standard track, athletes run 400 m but finish close to where they started, so their displacement is very small.
Pilots and ship navigators work with displacements (a distance plus a bearing) to plot courses between ports and airports.
A delivery driver's van records distance on its odometer; a GPS tracker can show the displacement from the depot at any moment.
examTips: Whenever a question asks for a displacement, always give a direction (north, left, upwards, or a sign) as well as a number and unit, or you may lose the mark.
Draw a quick sketch with arrows for back-and-forth journeys. Choose one direction as positive and add the movements with signs to find displacement.
If asked to explain the difference between distance and displacement, use the words scalar and vector and say that displacement has direction and is measured in a straight line from start to finish.
Check your answer: the size of the displacement can never be bigger than the distance travelled.
summary: Distance: how far an object moves; scalar; no direction.
Displacement: straight-line distance from start to finish plus direction; vector.
Displacement can be zero even when the distance travelled is large.
Size of displacement ≤ distance; equal only for straight-line motion in one direction.
Always give a direction with a displacement.

questions.question: Which statement describes displacement?
options: The total length of the path an object follows
The distance in a straight line from start to finish, with a direction
How fast an object moves in a given direction
The time taken to travel from start to finish
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector: straight-line distance from start to finish plus direction. A is distance, C is velocity, D is time.

questions.question: Which of these is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Distance has magnitude only. Displacement, velocity and force all have a direction, so they are vectors.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of displacement?
questions.explanation: Displacement is a length with a direction, so it is measured in metres. m/s is the unit of speed and velocity.

questions.question: Which is a correctly stated displacement?
questions.explanation: A displacement needs a magnitude with a length unit (m) and a direction. 12 m has no direction; m/s is a velocity unit; s is a time unit.

questions.question:
An object moves from point P to point Q.
When is the distance travelled equal to the size of the displacement?
options: The object moves in a straight line in one direction only
The object moves at a constant speed
The object follows a curved path
The object returns to P before reaching Q
questions.explanation: Any curve or reversal makes the path longer than the straight line from P to Q. Constant speed has nothing to do with the shape of the path.

questions.question:
A boy walks 120 m along a straight road to a shop. He then walks 50 m back towards his house.
Calculate the total distance the boy walks.
questions.explanation: Distance ignores direction: 120 + 50 = 170 m.

questions.question:
An athlete runs 2 complete laps of a 400 m track.
Calculate the distance the athlete runs.
questions.explanation: 2 × 400 = 800 m. Her displacement is zero because she finishes at the start line.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the movement of a lift. The lift starts at the ground floor.
Calculate the displacement of the lift from the ground floor at the end of stage 3.
questions.explanation: Taking up as positive: 15 − 6 + 9 = 18 m upwards. The distance travelled is 15 + 6 + 9 = 30 m.

questions.question:
A ball is thrown straight up. The ball rises 4.5 m and then falls back into the thrower's hand.
Calculate the distance travelled by the ball.
questions.explanation: The ball travels 4.5 m up and 4.5 m down, a total distance of 9.0 m. Its displacement is zero because it returns to the starting point.

Figure 1 shows the path of a drone. The drone flies 120 m due east and then 50 m due north.
Calculate the size of the displacement of the drone from its starting point.

figure.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 420 210" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="sans-serif"><line x1="390" y1="55" x2="390" y2="31.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><polygon points="390,25 393.6,32.1 386.4,32.1" fill="currentColor"/><text x="390" y="19" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">N</text><circle cx="60" cy="180" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="60" y="200" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">Start</text><line x1="60" y1="180" x2="302" y2="180" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.2"/><polygon points="310,180 301.1,184.5 301.1,175.5" fill="currentColor"/><text x="185" y="200" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">120 m</text><line x1="310" y1="180" x2="310" y2="83" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.2"/><polygon points="310,75 314.5,83.9 305.5,83.9" fill="currentColor"/><text x="320" y="130" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="start">50 m</text><circle cx="310" cy="75" r="4" fill="currentColor"/><text x="310" y="62" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">Finish</text><line x1="60" y1="180" x2="310" y2="75" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/></svg>

questions.explanation: The two movements are at right angles, so the displacement is the hypotenuse: √(120² + 50²) = √16 900 = 130 m (in a direction between east and north). The distance flown is 170 m.

questions.question: State whether distance is a scalar or a vector quantity.
questions.explanation: Distance has magnitude only and no direction, so it is a scalar.

questions.question: Give two differences between distance and displacement.
acceptedAnswers: distance is scalar, displacement is vector
displacement measured in a straight line from start to finish
markScheme: 1 mark: distance is a scalar / has no direction; displacement is a vector / has direction
1 mark: distance is the length of the path taken; displacement is measured in a straight line from start to finish
questions.explanation: The key ideas are scalar against vector, and path length against straight-line start-to-finish.

questions.question: Name one vector quantity other than displacement.
markScheme: 1 mark: any one of velocity, force, acceleration, weight, momentum
questions.explanation: These all have a direction. Speed, mass, time, energy and distance are scalars.

questions.question:
A train travels 30 km north from Town A to Town B. The train then returns 30 km south to Town A.
Give the distance travelled and the displacement of the train.
questions.explanation: The train covers 30 + 30 = 60 km, but it ends where it started, so its displacement is zero.

questions.question:
A student writes:
'The displacement of the car was 250 m.'
Explain why this statement is incomplete.
markScheme: 1 mark: so a direction must be given (for example 250 m west)
questions.explanation: Without a direction, 250 m only describes a distance (or the magnitude of the displacement).

questions.question: Explain why the size of the displacement of an object can never be greater than the distance it travels.
acceptedAnswers: shortest path is a straight line
displacement measured in a straight line
markScheme: 1 mark: displacement is measured along the straight line from start to finish
1 mark: a straight line is the shortest possible route, so any actual path is equal or longer
questions.explanation: The straight line between two points is the shortest path, so the real path (the distance) is always at least as long.

questions.question:
A swimmer swims 4 lengths of a 25 m pool. She finishes where she started.
What is the displacement of the swimmer?
questions.explanation: She finishes at her starting point, so the straight line from start to finish has zero length. The distance swum is 100 m.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the three stages of a walk by a hiker along a straight path.
Calculate the distance walked and the displacement of the hiker.
Give the direction of the displacement.
markScheme: 1 mark: taking east as positive, +2.0 − 5.0 + 1.0 = −2.0 km
questions.explanation: The negative result means the hiker finishes on the west side of the start. Many students forget to convert the negative sign into a direction.

questions.question:
Figure 1 shows a map of the route a student takes from her house to school. The school is north east of her house.
Compare the distance and displacement for her journey to school, and for the complete journey to school and back home again.

figure.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 420 230" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="sans-serif"><line x1="390" y1="55" x2="390" y2="31.4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><polygon points="390,25 393.6,32.1 386.4,32.1" fill="currentColor"/><text x="390" y="19" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">N</text><rect x="40" y="175" width="60" height="35" fill="#93c5fd" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="70" y="197" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">House</text><rect x="300" y="20" width="70" height="35" fill="#fde68a" fill-opacity="0.5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="335" y="42" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">School</text><path d="M100 190 H190 V120 H250 V70 H300 V40" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="3" stroke-opacity="0.5"/><text x="220" y="160" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="start">Route along roads = 1.8 km</text><line x1="100" y1="178" x2="300" y2="52" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><text x="150" y="105" font-size="12" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">Straight line = 1.2 km</text></svg>

markScheme: Distance to school is 1.8 km; distance is the length of the route taken
Displacement to school is 1.2 km north east; measured in a straight line with direction
Distance is larger because the road route is not a straight line
Distance is a scalar, displacement is a vector
For the return trip the distance is 3.6 km
For the return trip the displacement is zero because she ends at home
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear comparison for both journeys with correct values and reasoning
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct values or statements with little explanation
questions.explanation: A full answer gives values (1.8 km, 1.2 km NE, 3.6 km, 0) and explains why they differ using scalar and vector ideas.

questions.question:
A bus travels along a straight road. The bus moves 600 m east, stops, then reverses 50 m west into a bus stop.
Describe how to find the distance travelled and the displacement of the bus.
Explain why they are different.
markScheme: Distance: add the lengths of each part, ignoring direction: 600 + 50 = 650 m
Displacement: choose east as positive; +600 − 50 = +550 m
They differ because the bus changed direction
Distance is scalar so direction is ignored; displacement is a vector so movements in opposite directions partly cancel
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct method and values for both, with a reason for the difference
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one correct value or a basic statement of the difference
questions.explanation: Reversing direction is what makes distance and displacement differ for straight-line motion.

questions.question:
A ball is kicked from point S on a football pitch. It travels in a curved path through the air, bounces, and rolls to a stop at point T, 40 m north of S. Later a player kicks it from T back to S.
Explain, using the ideas of scalar and vector quantities, how the distance and displacement of the ball compare (a) for the motion from S to T and (b) for the whole motion from S to T and back to S. Suggest how each could be measured.
markScheme: Distance is a scalar: only magnitude; displacement is a vector: magnitude and direction
S to T: displacement is 40 m north (straight line from S to T)
S to T: distance is greater than 40 m because the path is curved (up through the air and bouncing)
Whole motion: displacement is zero because the ball ends at its starting point S
Whole motion: distance is the total length of both paths, more than 80 m
Displacement could be measured with a tape measure laid in a straight line from S to T and a compass for direction
Distance could be estimated by tracking the path, for example video analysis or adding up the lengths of each part of the path
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, correct comparison for both parts using scalar/vector terms with sensible measurement methods
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): correct comparison for at least one part with some explanation
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic statements, for example displacement has direction
questions.explanation: The key points are that a curved path makes distance exceed displacement, and returning to the start makes displacement zero while distance keeps growing.
